summary: A GGUF checkpoint's quantized matrices (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ1_S, IQ1_M, IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS, MXFP4) in the projections slot at their stored bits: decode rows on crit's kernel gguf-rows, prompt rows dequantized for cuBLAS or on gguf-rows' GEMM with the decode rows' bits
implementation_scope: The projections slot's host form over GGUF block formats (code/host.py: a Q8_0 encoder of dense rows, the stored values from Core's exact decoders crit_core.model.gguf_blocks, an exact-sum projection) and its device form (plugin.py): matrices loaded from the file's stored rows (GgufTensors), decode rows and expert stacks on crit's kernel gguf-rows' gemv, prompt rows either dequantized to BF16 for cuBLAS or on gguf-rows' gemm; the host-decoded BF16 values through torch where the kernel cannot be built. Every compute kernel is crit's gguf-rows or cuBLAS.

agent_guidance.use_when: An engine serves a GGUF checkpoint and its matrices are in the formats listed: decode reads the weights at their stored bits instead of a 16-bit copy
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The checkpoint's matrices are in other GGUF types (the ternary TQ1_0 and TQ2_0), or the engine fuses the projection with its neighbours in its own kernel
provides: gguf:<TYPE> matrices loaded from their stored rows, on the device at the stored size
Decode rows on dp4a over the stored blocks, each row's bits its own
An expert stack's rows each against their own expert (matmul_experts)
Prompt rows dequantized for cuBLAS, or with the decode rows' bits (prompt exact)
engine_supplies: The tensor names and which matrices to load, stack and permute (the file's converter may reorder some rows)
The checkpoint's dense tensors (norms, embeddings) and everything else in the model
preserve: The stored blocks as the file has them
A decode row's bits independent of the rows beside it
prompt exact: a prompt row's bits those of its decode row
adapt: Which prompt path a model takes, by its speed and the honesty its quality mode asks
Fusing the activation quantization into the norm before the projection

code_files.purpose: The host form: Q8_0 encoding of dense rows, the stored values from Core's decoders, the exact-sum projection

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ and numpy for the host form; a CUDA GPU (sm_80 on) with torch for the device form, crit's kernel gguf-rows where it builds
requires.model: A GGUF checkpoint whose matrices are Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ1_S, IQ1_M, IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS or MXFP4
requires.workload: Decode rows, verify windows and prompt chunks

contract.input: A matrix's stored rows uint8 [N][row bytes] (or [experts][N][row bytes]) with its format gguf:<TYPE>, or a dense weight as bf16; activations [tokens][K] in BF16, FP16 or FP32
contract.ownership: The plugin copies the stored rows to the device at load; the caller owns activations and outputs
contract.failure: Other formats, rows that are no whole number of the format's blocks and re-encoding requests raise ValueError at load
contract.core_boundary: Core reads the file's tensors (GgufTensors) and decodes the formats on the host (gguf_blocks); the model plugin chooses the tensors; this plugin multiplies

dependencies: crit's kernel gguf-rows (kernels/techniques/projections/gguf-rows) for the stored-bit paths

validation.host: Q8_0 encoding within half a block step of the dense rows; exact sums over the stored values
validation.native: tests/test_plugin.py on CUDA against gguf-rows' gemv and dequantize bit for bit, cuBLAS on the stored values, the decode rows' bits for exact prompt rows, expert stacks, the fallback
validation.performance: gguf-rows' README: decode rows at 71-96% of an RTX 5090's probed bandwidth; the dequantize prompt path at cuBLAS's BF16 speed plus one decode of the matrix a call
